== Biography ==
'''Elizabeth Glasgow''' was born about 1802 in County Antrim, Ireland. She married [[Anderson-104743|James Anderson]], and their children were baptised at the Rasharkin Presbyterian Church: [[Anderson-104744|Robert]] in 1834 and [[Anderson-104745|Hugh]] in 1836, recorded as the children of James Anderson and Betty/Elisabeth Glascaw of Drumack.<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 04 (28 July 1834) and 63 (24 November 1836), [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html transcription].</ref>

Elizabeth died at Gortahar, Rasharkin parish, on 7 September 1868, aged 66. The register describes her as a married farmer's wife who died of phthisis with no medical attendant. Her husband [[Anderson-104743|James Anderson]], who signed by mark, was present at her death at Gortahar; the death was registered on 29 September 1868.<ref name="ElizabethDeathGRONI">General Register Office for Northern Ireland, death register, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, entry 25, 7 September 1868: Elizabeth Anderson, Gortahar, female, married, 66, farmer's wife; cause phthisis, no medical attendant; informant James Anderson (his mark), present at death, Gortahar; registered 29 September 1868, John Thomson, registrar. Registration number D/1868/31/1005/2/25. Image viewed at [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/ GRONI online], 23 September 2026.</ref><ref>General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, 7 September 1868: Elizabeth Anderson, 66, Gortahar. "Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913", [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPTW-QQXN index record QPTW-QQXN].</ref>

Her sons [[Anderson-104792|David]], [[Anderson-104794|James]] and [[Anderson-104793|Samuel Anderson]] were farming at Gortahar in 1892, when they were named among the heirs and next of kin in the probate citation of her sister [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]] of Plattsburgh, New York.

=== Her husband's death ===
Her husband [[Anderson-104743|James Anderson]] died at Gortahar on 18 April 1888, a widower and retired farmer, reported age 94, of debility of three years' standing with no medical attendant. Their son [[Anderson-104794|James Anderson]] of Gortahar, who signed by mark, was present at the death and registered it on 4 May 1888.<ref name="JamesAndersonDeath1888">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, Ballymoney superintendent registrar's district, Dirraw registrar's district, 1888, entry 333: James Anderson, Gortahar, 18 April 1888; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1888/06179/4766465.pdf digital image], read 6 October 2026.</ref> The entry does not name his late wife; the townland, his widowed status, age and occupation, and the son's name identify him. The reported age implies birth about 1793–94. Elizabeth's probable brother [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] died in the same townland four weeks later.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-4090]] is assessed at 91% (proved). Elizabeth’s Gortahar Anderson sons link her family to Nancy’s 1892 probate kinship network. John of Lisnagaver’s 16 November 1846 marriage names father John Glasgow farmer; the maintained 6 October identity definition represents this father, extending the supported family hypothesis without requiring the 1796 flaxgrower match.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare full probate kinship wording with the Irish siblings’ own parent statements.

Source basis already held: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1846/09306/5369439.pdf Register image, IrishGenealogy.ie]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


No surviving record names Elizabeth's parents. She was a sister of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]] and of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]; the 1892 citation lists her sons "David Anderson, James Anderson and Samuel Anderson living at Gortahar" among Nancy's next of kin. Her parents are reassessed as [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]] (the father named in the 1846 marriage of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow of Lisnagaver]]) and an unknown mother, rather than Alexander Glasgow-3904 and Rosanna, to whom she was earlier attached.
